detail: the example contradicts the schema it illustrates: at `type`, `DumpCreation` is not one of the 13 values the enum allows. Generation is unaffected — an example is documentation — but a payload test built from this one is testing the document, not the generated code
`description` should be a string; kept the member verbatim and ignored it for generation

the property may be absent and may be null, and the document says those are different; both become `None`. The type is reached from a response body, so a caller cannot tell an explicit null from an absent member

the property may be absent and may be null, and the document says those are different; both become `None`. The type is reached from no operation's body, so nothing on the wire is affected, because no operation carries it

the property may be absent and may be null, and the document says those are different; both become `None`. The type is reached from a request body, so a caller cannot send an explicit null, which is how a request says `clear this` rather than `leave it alone`

the property may be absent and may be null, and the document says those are different; both become `None`. The type is reached from a request body and a response body, so a caller cannot send an explicit null, which is how a request says `clear this` rather than `leave it alone`
a schema in this position accepts no value at all, which no Rust type expresses
